```{r}
# =============================================================================
#
# FT-NIRS AGE PREDICTION - REPEATED 10-FOLD CROSS-VALIDATION FRAMEWORK
#
# This script performs repeated 10-fold cross-validation for five model types:
#   1. PCA-based models (Linear & GAM)
#   2. Partial Least Squares (PLS & PLS-VIP)
#   3. XGBoost
#   4. Random Forest
#   5. Simple biological models (Length + Structure Weight)
#
# The framework uses parallel processing to efficiently run hundreds of CV
# rounds, aggregating results at the round level to minimize memory usage.
#
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# SECTION 1: SETUP & DATA LOADING
# =============================================================================

# --- Load Required Packages ---
library(pacman)
p_load(
  caret,        # Machine learning utilities & preprocessing
  cowplot,      # Plot arrangements
  doParallel,   # Parallel backend
  doSNOW,       # Parallel progress tracking
  furrr,        # Parallel mapping with future
  future,       # Parallel computing framework
  gridExtra,    # Additional plot utilities
  mdatools,     # PLS modeling
  mgcv,         # GAM modeling
  MuMIn,        # Model selection (dredge)
  parallel,     # Core parallel utilities
  patchwork,    # Plot composition
  prospectr,    # Spectral preprocessing (Savitzky-Golay)
  purrr,        # Functional programming tools
  ranger,       # Random Forest implementation
  readxl,       # Excel file reading
  stringr,      # String manipulation
  tidyr,        # Data tidying
  tidyverse,    # Core tidyverse packages
  viridis,      # Color scales
  xgboost       # XGBoost modeling
)

# --- Load and Prepare Raw Data ---
df_raw <- readRDS("RDS_dataframes/combined_IBM_LPW_raw.RDS") %>% 
  filter(complete.cases(read_age))

# Consolidate regional groupings
df_raw <- df_raw %>%
  mutate(
    region = case_when(
      region %in% c("E Shumagins", "W Shumagins") ~ "Shumagin",
      region %in% c("N Kodiak", "S Kodiak") ~ "Kodiak",
      TRUE ~ region
    )
  )

# Create region-specific datasets
kodiak_raw <- df_raw %>% filter(region == "Kodiak")
shumagin_raw <- df_raw %>% filter(region == "Shumagin")
lpw_raw <- df_raw %>% filter(region == "LPW")


```

```{r}

# =============================================================================
# SECTION 2: UTILITY FUNCTIONS
# =============================================================================

# --- 2.1: Data Manipulation Functions ---

#' Find spectral column names
#' 
#' Identifies columns containing wavenumber data (numeric column names)
#' @param df Dataframe containing spectral data
#' @return Character vector of spectral column names
find_cols <- function(df) {
  names(df)[grepl("^\\d", names(df))]
}

#' Convert spectral data to long format
#' 
#' Transforms wide-format spectral data into long format for visualization
#' @param df Dataframe with spectral columns
#' @return Long-format dataframe with 'name' (wavenumber) and 'value' columns
make_long <- function(df) {
  speccols <- find_cols(df)
  df_long <- df %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = speccols) %>%
    mutate(name = as.numeric(as.character(name)))
  return(df_long)
}


# --- 2.2: Data Splitting Functions ---

#' Generate stratified cross-validation splits
#' 
#' Creates multiple sets of 10-fold CV splits, stratified by age and region.
#' For multi-region data, ensures each fold contains samples from all regions.
#' For single-region data, reduces to simple age-stratified splits.
#' 
#' @param data Full dataset
#' @param n_splits Number of independent CV repetitions to create
#' @param strata_col Column name for stratification (default: "read_age")
#' @param group_col Column name for grouping (default: "region")
#' @return List of length n_splits, each containing 10 fold index lists
generate_multiple_splits <- function(data, n_splits,
                                     strata_col = "read_age",
                                     group_col = "region") {
  
  regions <- unique(data[[group_col]])
  
  purrr::map(1:n_splits, function(split_num) {
    
    # Create stratified folds within each region
    region_folds <- purrr::map(regions, function(reg) {
      region_data <- data[data[[group_col]] == reg, ]
      region_indices <- which(data[[group_col]] == reg)
      
      folds <- caret::createFolds(
        region_data[[strata_col]],
        k = 10,
        list = TRUE,
        returnTrain = FALSE
      )
      
      # Convert local indices to global indices
      purrr::map(folds, ~ region_indices[.x])
    })
    
    # Combine corresponding folds across regions
    # (Fold 1 = Region1_Fold1 + Region2_Fold1 + ...)
    combined_folds <- purrr::map(1:10, function(fold_num) {
      unlist(purrr::map(region_folds, fold_num))
    })
    
    names(combined_folds) <- paste0("Fold", sprintf("%02d", 1:10))
    combined_folds
  })
}


# --- 2.3: Spectral Preprocessing Functions ---

#' Apply Savitzky-Golay smoothing filter
#' 
#' @param df Dataframe with spectral columns
#' @param m Derivative order (0 = smoothing only, 1 = first derivative, etc.)
#' @param p Polynomial order
#' @param w Window size (must be odd)
#' @return Dataframe with filtered spectral data
sg_filter <- function(df, m, p, w) {
  speccols <- find_cols(df)
  metacols <- setdiff(names(df), speccols)
  sg_matrix <- prospectr::savitzkyGolay(df[, speccols], m = m, p = p, w = w)
  new_speccols <- find_cols(sg_matrix)
  names(sg_matrix) <- new_speccols
  return(dplyr::bind_cols(df[, metacols], as.data.frame(sg_matrix)))
}

#' Apply Standard Normal Variate (SNV) transformation
#' 
#' Centers and scales each spectrum to correct for scatter effects
#' @param df Dataframe with spectral columns
#' @return Dataframe with SNV-transformed spectral data
snv_filter <- function(df) {
  speccols <- find_cols(df)
  metacols <- setdiff(names(df), speccols)
  snv_matrix <- prospectr::prep.snv(as.matrix(df[, speccols]))
  return(dplyr::bind_cols(df[, metacols], as.data.frame(snv_matrix)))
}

#' Filter spectral data by wavelength threshold
#' 
#' Removes wavenumbers above a specified threshold
#' @param df Dataframe with spectral columns
#' @param wave Maximum wavenumber to retain
#' @return Dataframe with filtered wavelength range
wave_filter <- function(df, wave) {
  speccols <- find_cols(df)
  metacols <- setdiff(names(df), speccols)
  keep_me <- as.numeric(speccols) <= wave
  speccols_keep <- speccols[keep_me]
  return(df[, c(metacols, speccols_keep)])
}


# --- 2.4: Model Performance Metrics ---

#' Calculate Ratio of Performance to Deviation (RPD)
#' 
#' RPD = SD(observed) / RMSE
#' Higher values indicate better model performance
calculate_rpd <- function(observed, predicted) {
  sd(observed) / sqrt(mean((observed - predicted)^2))
}

#' Calculate prediction bias
#' 
#' Bias = mean(predicted - observed)
#' Positive = over-prediction, Negative = under-prediction
calculate_bias <- function(observed, predicted) {
  mean(predicted - observed)
}


# --- 2.5: PCA Helper Functions ---

#' Extract PC indices from linear model terms
#' 
#' @param term Terms object from an lm() model
#' @return Numeric vector of PC indices used in the model
get_pc_indices_lm <- function(term) {
  as.numeric(stringr::str_extract(attr(term, "term.labels"), "\\d+"))
}

#' Extract PC indices from GAM formula
#' 
#' @param formula Formula object from a gam() model
#' @return Numeric vector of PC indices used in the model
get_pc_indices_gam <- function(formula) {
  pc_matches <- stringr::str_extract_all(as.character(formula)[3], "PC\\d+")[[1]]
  as.numeric(stringr::str_extract(pc_matches, "\\d+"))
}

#' Calculate importance as vector length in PC space
#' 
#' For a given set of PCs, calculates the Euclidean length of the loading
#' vector for each wavenumber. Longer vectors = more important wavenumbers.
#' 
#' @param pca_rotation PCA rotation matrix (loadings)
#' @param pc_indices Which PCs to include in calculation
#' @return Numeric vector of importance scores (one per wavenumber)
calculate_pca_vector_length <- function(pca_rotation, pc_indices) {
  if (length(pc_indices) == 0 || is.null(pc_indices)) {
    return(rep(0, nrow(pca_rotation)))
  }
  valid_indices <- pc_indices[!is.na(pc_indices)]
  if (length(valid_indices) == 0) {
    return(rep(0, nrow(pca_rotation)))
  }
  loadings_subset <- pca_rotation[, valid_indices, drop = FALSE]
  sqrt(rowSums(loadings_subset^2))
}


# --- 2.6: Result Aggregation Functions ---

#' Summarize variable importance by CV round
#' 
#' Aggregates importance values across 10 folds within each round,
#' reducing memory usage by ~10x while preserving key statistics
#' 
#' @param importance_df Raw importance data with round and fold columns
#' @return Summarized dataframe with mean and SD per round
summarize_importance_by_round <- function(importance_df) {
  importance_df %>%
    group_by(model_type, model_name, wavenumber, round) %>%
    summarize(
      importance_mean = mean(importance, na.rm = TRUE),
      importance_sd = sd(importance, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_folds = n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}


# --- 2.7: Visualization Functions ---

#' Create spectral plot
#' 
#' Generates a line plot of absorbance vs wavenumber for multiple specimens
#' @param df Dataframe with spectral data
#' @param color Column name (unquoted) to use for coloring lines
#' @return ggplot object
spec.fig <- function(df, color) {
  mydf <- make_long(df)
  color_col <- rlang::enquo(color) 
  
  mydf_sorted <- mydf %>% 
    dplyr::arrange(specimen, name) 
  
  ggplot(mydf_sorted) +
    geom_path(aes(x = name, y = value, color = !!color_col, group = specimen)) +
    scale_x_reverse() +
    scale_color_viridis() +
    labs(y = "Absorbance", x = expression(paste("Wavenumber ", cm^-1))) + 
    theme_bw(base_size = 16)
}


```


```{r}
# =============================================================================
# SECTION 3: INDIVIDUAL MODEL RUNNER FUNCTIONS
# =============================================================================
# Each function fits one model type to calibration data and evaluates on test data
# All functions return a list with: metrics, predictions, and importance (if applicable)

# --- 3.1: PCA-Based Models (LM & GAM) ---

#' Run PCA-based linear and GAM models
#' 
#' Fits 10 pre-selected LM models and 10 pre-selected GAM models on PC scores
#' 
#' @param cal_df Calibration data
#' @param test_df Test data  
#' @param terms_lm List of 10 formula terms for linear models
#' @param terms_gam List of 10 formulas for GAM models
#' @return List containing metrics, predictions, and importance dataframes
run_pca_models <- function(cal_df, test_df, terms_lm, terms_gam) {
  spec_cols <- find_cols(cal_df)
  
  # Perform PCA on calibration data
  pc.mod <- caret::preProcess(
    cal_df[, spec_cols],
    method = c("center", "pca"),
    pcaComp = 10
  )
  
  # Transform both datasets to PC space
  cal_pca <- cbind(predict(pc.mod, cal_df[, spec_cols]), cal_df)
  test_pca <- cbind(predict(pc.mod, test_df[, spec_cols]), test_df)
  
  # --- Fit 10 Linear Models ---
  metrics_lm_list <- list()
  preds_lm_list <- list()
  importance_lm_list <- list()
  
  for (j in 1:10) {
    mod_name <- paste("PCA-LM", j)
    mod <- lm(data = cal_pca, terms_lm[[j]])
    preds <- predict(mod, newdata = test_pca)
    
    # Store metrics
    metrics_lm_list[[j]] <- data.frame(
      model_type = "PCA-LM",
      model_name = mod_name,
      R2 = 1 - (sum((test_pca$read_age - preds)^2) / 
                  sum((test_pca$read_age - mean(test_pca$read_age))^2)),
      RMSE = caret::RMSE(pred = preds, obs = test_pca$read_age),
      RPD = calculate_rpd(test_pca$read_age, preds),
      Bias = calculate_bias(test_pca$read_age, preds)
    )
    
    # Store predictions
    preds_lm_list[[j]] <- data.frame(
      specimen = test_pca$specimen,
      obs_age = test_pca$read_age,
      pred_age = preds,
      model_type = "PCA-LM",
      model_name = mod_name
    )
    
    # Calculate importance based on PC loadings
    pc_indices <- get_pc_indices_lm(terms_lm[[j]])
    importance_lm_list[[j]] <- data.frame(
      model_type = "PCA-LM",
      model_name = mod_name,
      wavenumber = as.numeric(rownames(pc.mod$rotation)),
      importance = calculate_pca_vector_length(pc.mod$rotation, pc_indices)
    )
  }
  
  # --- Fit 10 GAM Models ---
  metrics_gam_list <- list()
  preds_gam_list <- list()
  importance_gam_list <- list()
  
  for (j in 1:10) {
    mod_name <- paste("PCA-GAM", j)
    mod <- mgcv::gam(data = cal_pca, terms_gam[[j]], method = "REML")
    preds <- predict(mod, newdata = test_pca)
    
    metrics_gam_list[[j]] <- data.frame(
      model_type = "PCA-GAM",
      model_name = mod_name,
      R2 = 1 - (sum((test_pca$read_age - preds)^2) / 
                  sum((test_pca$read_age - mean(test_pca$read_age))^2)),
      RMSE = caret::RMSE(pred = preds, obs = test_pca$read_age),
      RPD = calculate_rpd(test_pca$read_age, preds),
      Bias = calculate_bias(test_pca$read_age, preds)
    )
    
    preds_gam_list[[j]] <- data.frame(
      specimen = test_pca$specimen,
      obs_age = test_pca$read_age,
      pred_age = preds,
      model_type = "PCA-GAM",
      model_name = mod_name
    )
    
    pc_indices <- get_pc_indices_gam(terms_gam[[j]])
    importance_gam_list[[j]] <- data.frame(
      model_type = "PCA-GAM",
      model_name = mod_name,
      wavenumber = as.numeric(rownames(pc.mod$rotation)),
      importance = calculate_pca_vector_length(pc.mod$rotation, pc_indices)
    )
  }
  
  # Combine all results
  return(list(
    metrics = bind_rows(metrics_lm_list, metrics_gam_list),
    predictions = bind_rows(preds_lm_list, preds_gam_list),
    importance = bind_rows(importance_lm_list, importance_gam_list)
  ))
}


# --- 3.2: PLS Models (Standard & VIP-Selected) ---

#' Run PLS and PLS-VIP models
#' 
#' Fits two PLS models: (1) standard PLS, (2) PLS with VIP variable selection
#' 
#' @param cal_df Calibration data
#' @param test_df Test data
#' @param vip_threshold VIP score threshold for variable selection (default: 1.0)
#' @return List containing metrics, predictions, and importance dataframes
run_pls_models <- function(cal_df, test_df, vip_threshold = 1.0) {
  spec_cols <- find_cols(cal_df)
  
  Xc <- as.matrix(cal_df[, spec_cols])
  Yc <- as.matrix(cal_df$read_age)
  Xt <- as.matrix(test_df[, spec_cols])
  Yt <- as.matrix(test_df$read_age)
  
  # --- Model 1: Standard PLS ---
  mod_pls <- mdatools::pls(
    Xc, Yc,
    cv = 1,  # LOOCV for component selection
    scale = FALSE,
    center = TRUE,
    x.test = Xt,
    y.test = Yt
  )
  ncomp_pls <- mod_pls$ncomp.selected
  vip_scores <- mdatools::vipscores(mod_pls, ncomp = ncomp_pls)
  
  # --- Model 2: PLS with VIP Selection ---
  excl_cols_vip <- which(vip_scores < vip_threshold)
  
  mod_vip <- mdatools::pls(
    Xc, Yc,
    cv = 1,
    scale = FALSE,
    center = TRUE,
    x.test = Xt,
    y.test = Yt,
    exclcols = excl_cols_vip
  )
  ncomp_vip <- mod_vip$ncomp.selected
  
  # Compile results
  metrics <- bind_rows(
    data.frame(
      model_type = "PLS",
      model_name = "PLS",
      R2 = mod_pls$testres$r2[ncomp_pls],
      RMSE = mod_pls$testres$rmse[ncomp_pls],
      RPD = mod_pls$testres$rpd[ncomp_pls],
      Bias = mod_pls$testres$bias[ncomp_pls]
    ),
    data.frame(
      model_type = "PLS-VIP",
      model_name = paste0("PLS-VIP (>", vip_threshold, ")"),
      R2 = mod_vip$testres$r2[ncomp_vip],
      RMSE = mod_vip$testres$rmse[ncomp_vip],
      RPD = mod_vip$testres$rpd[ncomp_vip],
      Bias = mod_vip$testres$bias[ncomp_vip]
    )
  )
  
  predictions <- bind_rows(
    data.frame(
      specimen = test_df$specimen,
      obs_age = Yt,
      pred_age = mod_pls$testres$y.pred[, ncomp_pls, 1],
      model_type = "PLS",
      model_name = "PLS"
    ),
    data.frame(
      specimen = test_df$specimen,
      obs_age = Yt,
      pred_age = mod_vip$testres$y.pred[, ncomp_vip, 1],
      model_type = "PLS-VIP",
      model_name = paste0("PLS-VIP (>", vip_threshold, ")")
    )
  )
  
  importance <- data.frame(
    model_type = "PLS-VIP",
    model_name = "PLS-VIP",
    wavenumber = as.numeric(colnames(Xc)),
    importance = as.vector(vip_scores)
  )
  
  return(list(
    metrics = metrics,
    predictions = predictions,
    importance = importance
  ))
}


# --- 3.3: XGBoost Model ---

#' Run XGBoost gradient boosting model
#' 
#' Uses pre-tuned hyperparameters to fit an XGBoost regression model
#' 
#' @param cal_df Calibration data
#' @param test_df Test data
#' @param best_params_xgb Dataframe with tuned hyperparameters
#' @return List containing metrics, predictions, and importance dataframes
run_xgb_model <- function(cal_df, test_df, best_params_xgb) {
  spec_cols <- find_cols(cal_df)
  
  # Prepare DMatrix objects
  dtrain <- xgb.DMatrix(
    data = as.matrix(cal_df[, spec_cols]),
    label = cal_df$read_age
  )
  dtest <- xgb.DMatrix(
    data = as.matrix(test_df[, spec_cols]),
    label = test_df$read_age
  )
  
  # Set model parameters from pre-tuned values
  params <- list(
    objective = "reg:squarederror",
    booster = "gbtree",
    nthread = 1,
    eta = best_params_xgb$eta,
    max_depth = best_params_xgb$max_depth,
    min_child_weight = best_params_xgb$min_child_weight,
    subsample = best_params_xgb$subsample,
    gamma = best_params_xgb$gamma,
    colsample_bytree = best_params_xgb$colsample_bytree
  )
  best_nrounds <- round(best_params_xgb$mean_nrounds)
  
  # Train model
  mod_xgb <- xgb.train(
    params = params,
    data = dtrain,
    nrounds = best_nrounds,
    verbose = 0
  )
  
  # Generate predictions
  preds <- predict(mod_xgb, dtest)
  obs <- test_df$read_age
  
  RSS <- sum((obs - preds)^2)
  TSS <- sum((obs - mean(obs))^2)
  
  metrics <- data.frame(
    model_type = "XGB", model_name = "XGBoost",
    R2 = 1 - (RSS / TSS),  # <-- CORRECTED
    RMSE = caret::RMSE(pred = preds, obs = obs),
    RPD = calculate_rpd(obs, preds), 
    Bias = calculate_bias(obs, preds)
  )
  
  predictions <- data.frame(
    specimen = test_df$specimen,
    obs_age = obs,
    pred_age = preds,
    model_type = "XGB",
    model_name = "XGBoost"
  )
  
  # Extract feature importance (Gain)
  imp_matrix <- xgb.importance(model = mod_xgb)
  imp_df <- data.frame(Feature = colnames(cal_df[, spec_cols])) %>%
    left_join(imp_matrix, by = "Feature") %>%
    mutate(
      model_type = "XGB",
      model_name = "XGBoost",
      wavenumber = as.numeric(Feature),
      importance = ifelse(is.na(Gain), 0, Gain)
    ) %>%
    select(model_type, model_name, wavenumber, importance)
  
  return(list(
    metrics = metrics,
    predictions = predictions,
    importance = imp_df
  ))
}


# --- 3.4: Random Forest Model ---

#' Run Random Forest regression model
#' 
#' Uses pre-tuned hyperparameters to fit a ranger Random Forest model
#' 
#' @param cal_df Calibration data
#' @param test_df Test data
#' @param best_params_rf Dataframe with tuned hyperparameters
#' @return List containing metrics, predictions, and importance dataframes
run_rf_model <- function(cal_df, test_df, best_params_rf) {
  spec_cols <- find_cols(cal_df)
  
  # Train Random Forest
  mod_rf <- ranger::ranger(
    x = cal_df[, spec_cols],
    y = cal_df$read_age,
    mtry = best_params_rf$mtry,
    min.node.size = best_params_rf$min.node.size,
    splitrule = "variance",
    importance = 'permutation',
    num.trees = 1000,
    num.threads = 1
  )
  
  # Generate predictions
  preds <- predict(mod_rf, data = test_df)$predictions
  obs <- test_df$read_age
  
  
  RSS <- sum((obs - preds)^2)
  TSS <- sum((obs - mean(obs))^2)
  
  metrics <- data.frame(
    model_type = "RF", model_name = "Random Forest",
    R2 = 1 - (RSS / TSS), # <-- CORRECTED
    RMSE = caret::RMSE(pred = preds, obs = obs),
    RPD = calculate_rpd(obs, preds), 
    Bias = calculate_bias(obs, preds)
  )
  
  predictions <- data.frame(
    specimen = test_df$specimen,
    obs_age = obs,
    pred_age = preds,
    model_type = "RF",
    model_name = "Random Forest"
  )
  
  importance <- data.frame(
    model_type = "RF",
    model_name = "Random Forest",
    wavenumber = as.numeric(names(mod_rf$variable.importance)),
    importance = as.vector(mod_rf$variable.importance)
  )
  
  return(list(
    metrics = metrics,
    predictions = predictions,
    importance = importance
  ))
}


# --- 3.5: Simple Biological Models ---

#' Run simple models using only biological measurements
#' 
#' Fits linear and GAM models using length and structure weight only
#' (no spectral data). Useful as baseline comparison models.
#' 
#' @param cal_df Calibration data
#' @param test_df Test data
#' @return List containing metrics and predictions (no importance)
run_simple_models <- function(cal_df, test_df) {
  bio_vars <- c("read_age", "length", "structure_weight")
  
  # Remove rows with missing biological data
  cal_simple <- cal_df[complete.cases(cal_df[, bio_vars]), ]
  test_simple <- test_df[complete.cases(test_df[, bio_vars]), ]
  
  if (nrow(cal_simple) == 0 || nrow(test_simple) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # --- Model 1: Simple Linear Model ---
  mod_lm <- lm(read_age ~ length + structure_weight, data = cal_simple)
  preds_lm <- predict(mod_lm, newdata = test_simple)
  obs <- test_simple$read_age
  
  
  RSS_lm <- sum((obs - preds_lm)^2)
  TSS_lm <- sum((obs - mean(obs))^2)
  
  metrics_lm <- data.frame(
    model_type = "Simple", model_name = "Simple-LM (L+SW)",
    R2 = 1 - (RSS_lm / TSS_lm), # <-- CORRECTED
    RMSE = caret::RMSE(pred = preds_lm, obs = obs), # <-- ADDED RMSE
    RPD = calculate_rpd(obs, preds_lm), 
    Bias = calculate_bias(obs, preds_lm)
  )
  
  preds_lm_df <- data.frame(
    specimen = test_simple$specimen,
    obs_age = obs,
    pred_age = preds_lm,
    model_type = "Simple",
    model_name = "Simple-LM (L+SW)"
  )
  
  # --- Model 2: Simple GAM ---
  mod_gam <- mgcv::gam(
    read_age ~ s(length, k = 4) + s(structure_weight, k = 4),
    data = cal_simple,
    method = "REML"
  )
  preds_gam <- predict(mod_gam, newdata = test_simple)
  
  
  
   RSS_gam <- sum((obs - preds_gam)^2)
   TSS_gam <- sum((obs - mean(obs))^2)
  
  metrics_gam <- data.frame(
    model_type = "Simple", model_name = "Simple-GAM (L+SW)",
    R2 = 1 - (RSS_gam / TSS_gam), # <-- CORRECTED
    RMSE = caret::RMSE(pred = preds_gam, obs = obs),
    RPD = calculate_rpd(obs, preds_gam), 
    Bias = calculate_bias(obs, preds_gam)
  )
  
  preds_gam_df <- data.frame(
    specimen = test_simple$specimen,
    obs_age = obs,
    pred_age = preds_gam,
    model_type = "Simple",
    model_name = "Simple-GAM (L+SW)"
  )
  
  return(list(
    metrics = bind_rows(metrics_lm, metrics_gam),
    predictions = bind_rows(preds_lm_df, preds_gam_df),
    importance = data.frame()  # No importance for simple models
  ))
}

```



```{r}
# =============================================================================
# SECTION 4: CROSS-VALIDATION WORKER FUNCTIONS
# =============================================================================

# --- 4.1: Single Fold Worker ---

#' Run all models for a single CV fold
#' 
#' Worker function that fits all 5 model types on one train/test split.
#' Called repeatedly within each CV round.
#' 
#' @param cal_indices Row indices for calibration set
#' @param test_indices Row indices for test set
#' @param full_df Complete dataset
#' @param terms_lm Pre-selected LM model formulas
#' @param terms_gam Pre-selected GAM model formulas
#' @param best_params_xgb Tuned XGBoost parameters
#' @param best_params_rf Tuned Random Forest parameters
#' @param vip_threshold VIP score cutoff for PLS variable selection
#' @return List with metrics, predictions, and importance for all models
run_all_models_for_fold <- function(cal_indices, test_indices,
                                    full_df,
                                    terms_lm, terms_gam,
                                    best_params_xgb, best_params_rf,
                                    vip_threshold = 1.0) {
  
  # Subset data for this fold
  cal_df <- full_df[cal_indices, ]
  test_df <- full_df[test_indices, ]
  
  # Initialize result containers
  metrics_list <- list()
  predictions_list <- list()
  importance_list <- list()
  
  # Run each model type with error handling
  tryCatch({
    pca_results <- run_pca_models(cal_df, test_df, terms_lm, terms_gam)
    metrics_list$pca <- pca_results$metrics
    predictions_list$pca <- pca_results$predictions
    importance_list$pca <- pca_results$importance
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("PCA Models FAILED for a fold: ", e$message)
  })
  
  tryCatch({
    pls_results <- run_pls_models(cal_df, test_df, vip_threshold)
    metrics_list$pls <- pls_results$metrics
    predictions_list$pls <- pls_results$predictions
    importance_list$pls <- pls_results$importance
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("PLS Models FAILED for a fold: ", e$message)
  })
  
  tryCatch({
    xgb_results <- run_xgb_model(cal_df, test_df, best_params_xgb)
    metrics_list$xgb <- xgb_results$metrics
    predictions_list$xgb <- xgb_results$predictions
    importance_list$xgb <- xgb_results$importance
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("XGBoost Model FAILED for a fold: ", e$message)
  })
  
  tryCatch({
    rf_results <- run_rf_model(cal_df, test_df, best_params_rf)
    metrics_list$rf <- rf_results$metrics
    predictions_list$rf <- rf_results$predictions
    importance_list$rf <- rf_results$importance
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Random Forest Model FAILED for a fold: ", e$message)
  })
  
  tryCatch({
    simple_results <- run_simple_models(cal_df, test_df)
    if (!is.null(simple_results)) {
      metrics_list$simple <- simple_results$metrics
      predictions_list$simple <- simple_results$predictions
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    message("Simple Models FAILED for a fold: ", e$message)
  })
  
  # Combine all results for this fold
  all_metrics <- bind_rows(metrics_list)
  all_predictions <- bind_rows(predictions_list)
  all_importance <- bind_rows(importance_list)
  
  return(list(
    metrics = all_metrics,
    predictions = all_predictions,
    importance = all_importance
  ))
}


# --- 4.2: Round-Level Worker (Memory-Efficient Aggregation) ---

#' Process one complete CV round (10 folds)
#' 
#' Runs all 10 folds for a single round sequentially, then aggregates
#' the results BEFORE returning. This is the key memory-saving step:
#' instead of returning 10 large result objects, we return 3 small summaries.
#' 
#' @param round_num The current round number (for tracking)
#' @param test_folds_for_this_round List of 10 test index vectors
#' @param cal_folds_for_this_round List of 10 calibration index vectors
#' @param full_df Complete dataset
#' @param terms_lm Pre-selected LM model formulas
#' @param terms_gam Pre-selected GAM model formulas
#' @param best_params_xgb Tuned XGBoost parameters
#' @param best_params_rf Tuned Random Forest parameters
#' @param vip_threshold VIP score cutoff for PLS variable selection
#' @return List with aggregated metrics_summary, importance_summary, and raw predictions
# UPDATED: Keep predictions but make them more memory-efficient



process_one_round <- function(round_num,
                              test_folds_for_this_round,
                              cal_folds_for_this_round,
                              full_df,
                              terms_lm, terms_gam,
                              best_params_xgb, best_params_rf,
                              vip_threshold = 1.0) {

  # --- Step 1: Run all 10 folds sequentially ---
  fold_results_list <- purrr::map(1:10, function(fold_num) {
    run_all_models_for_fold(
      cal_indices = cal_folds_for_this_round[[fold_num]],
      test_indices = test_folds_for_this_round[[fold_num]],
      full_df = full_df,
      terms_lm = terms_lm,
      terms_gam = terms_gam,
      best_params_xgb = best_params_xgb,
      best_params_rf = best_params_rf,
      vip_threshold = vip_threshold
    )
  })

  # --- Step 2: Aggregate metrics (average across 10 folds) ---
  metrics_summary <- purrr::map_dfr(fold_results_list, "metrics") %>%
    group_by(model_type, model_name) %>%
    summarize(
      R2 = mean(R2, na.rm = TRUE),
      RMSE = mean(RMSE, na.rm = TRUE),
      RPD = mean(RPD, na.rm = TRUE),
      Bias = mean(Bias, na.rm = TRUE),
      round = round_num,  # Add round here, inside summarize
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  # --- Step 3: Aggregate importance (average across 10 folds) ---
  importance_raw <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(fold_results_list), function(i) {
    fold_results_list[[i]]$importance %>%
      mutate(fold = i, round = round_num)
  })

  importance_summary <- summarize_importance_by_round(importance_raw)

  # --- Step 4: Collect all predictions (no aggregation) ---
  predictions_raw <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(fold_results_list), function(i) {
    fold_results_list[[i]]$predictions %>%
      mutate(round = round_num, fold = i)
  })

  # Return compact, summarized data
  return(list(
    metrics_summary = metrics_summary,
    importance_summary = importance_summary,
    predictions_raw = predictions_raw
  ))
}
```


```{r}
# =============================================================================
# SECTION 5: MAIN PARALLEL CV ORCHESTRATION
# =============================================================================

#' Run complete repeated cross-validation analysis
#' 
#' Master function that orchestrates the entire repeated CV process.
#' Splits are parallelized at the ROUND level (not fold level) to
#' enable efficient memory-saving aggregation.
#' 
#' @param df Dataset to analyze
#' @param num_rounds Number of independent CV repetitions
#' @param terms_lm Pre-selected LM model formulas
#' @param terms_gam Pre-selected GAM model formulas
#' @param best_params_xgb Tuned XGBoost parameters
#' @param best_params_rf Tuned Random Forest parameters
#' @param vip_threshold VIP score cutoff for PLS variable selection
#' @param n_cores Number of CPU cores for parallel processing
#' @return List with all_cv_metrics, all_cv_predictions, all_cv_importance

run_all_models_cv <- function(df, num_rounds, terms_lm, terms_gam,
                              best_params_xgb, best_params_rf,
                              vip_threshold = 1.0, n_cores = 8) {

  cli::cli_h1(paste("Starting Repeated CV for", deparse(substitute(df))))

  # --- Step 1: Generate all train/test splits ---
  cli::cli_alert_info(paste("Generating", num_rounds * 10, "CV fold jobs..."))

  test.idx_nested <- generate_multiple_splits(df, num_rounds)

  cal.idx_nested <- purrr::map(test.idx_nested, ~ {
    purrr::map(., ~ setdiff(1:nrow(df), .))
  })

  # --- Step 2: Run all rounds in parallel ---
  cli::cli_alert_info(paste("Running", num_rounds, "rounds on", n_cores, "cores..."))

  plan(multisession, workers = n_cores)

  # Create a list of round indices to iterate over
  round_indices <- seq_along(test.idx_nested)

  all_round_results_list <- furrr::future_pmap(
    .l = list(
      test_folds = test.idx_nested,
      cal_folds = cal.idx_nested,
      round_num = round_indices
    ),
    .f = function(test_folds, cal_folds, round_num) {
      process_one_round(
        round_num = round_num,
        test_folds_for_this_round = test_folds,
        cal_folds_for_this_round = cal_folds,
        full_df = df,
        terms_lm = terms_lm,
        terms_gam = terms_gam,
        best_params_xgb = best_params_xgb,
        best_params_rf = best_params_rf,
        vip_threshold = vip_threshold
      )
    },
    .options = furrr_options(
      seed = TRUE,
      packages = c("dplyr", "purrr", "mgcv", "caret", "mdatools", "ranger", "xgboost")
    )
  )

  plan(sequential)
  cli::cli_alert_success("Parallel CV execution complete.")

  # --- Step 3: Aggregate all round-level results ---
  cli::cli_alert_info("Aggregating round-level results...")

  all_cv_metrics <- purrr::map_dfr(all_round_results_list, "metrics_summary")
  all_cv_importance <- purrr::map_dfr(all_round_results_list, "importance_summary")
  all_cv_predictions <- purrr::map_dfr(all_round_results_list, "predictions_raw")

  # Free memory
  rm(all_round_results_list)
  gc()

  cli::cli_alert_success("Aggregation complete.")

  # Return final results
  return(list(
    all_cv_metrics = all_cv_metrics,
    all_cv_predictions = all_cv_predictions,
    all_cv_importance = all_cv_importance
  ))
}
```


```{r}
# =============================================================================
# SECTION 6: HIGH-LEVEL EXPERIMENT RUNNER
# =============================================================================

#' Run complete modeling experiment with model selection
#' 
#' Top-level function that handles:
#'   1. Model selection via dredge (finds best PCA-based models)
#'   2. Repeated cross-validation
#'   3. Result summarization and saving
#' 
#' @param df_to_run Dataset to analyze
#' @param save_prefix Prefix for output filenames
#' @param num_rounds Number of CV repetitions
#' @param best_params_xgb Tuned XGBoost parameters
#' @param best_params_rf Tuned Random Forest parameters
#' @param vip_threshold VIP score cutoff for PLS
#' @param n_cores Number of CPU cores
#' @return List with all CV results
run_experiment <- function(df_to_run,
                           save_prefix,
                           num_rounds,
                           best_params_xgb,
                           best_params_rf,
                           vip_threshold = 1.0,
                           n_cores = 8) {
  
  # --- Step 1: Model selection via dredge ---
  cli::cli_h1(paste("Running Dredge Pre-computation for:", save_prefix))
  
  pca_spec_cols <- find_cols(df_to_run)
  
  # Perform PCA on full dataset for model selection
  dredge_pc.mod <- caret::preProcess(
    df_to_run[, pca_spec_cols],
    method = c("center", "pca"),
    pcaComp = 10
  )
  
  dredge_cal_pca <- cbind(
    predict(dredge_pc.mod, df_to_run[, pca_spec_cols]),
    df_to_run
  )
  
  dredge_model_data <- dredge_cal_pca[, c("read_age", paste0("PC", 1:10))]
  
  # Build global models for dredging
  dredge_global_lm <- lm(
    read_age ~ .,
    data = dredge_model_data,
    na.action = "na.fail",
    model = TRUE
  )
  
  dredge_global_gam <- mgcv::gam(
    read_age ~ s(PC1, k = 4) + s(PC2, k = 4) + s(PC3, k = 4) + 
      s(PC4, k = 4) + s(PC5, k = 4) + s(PC6, k = 4) + 
      s(PC7, k = 4) + s(PC8, k = 4) + s(PC9, k = 4) + s(PC10, k = 4),
    data = dredge_model_data,
    na.action = "na.fail",
    model = TRUE
  )
  
  # Attach data to model environments (required for dredge)
  attr(dredge_global_lm$terms, ".Environment") <- 
    list2env(list(dredge_model_data = dredge_model_data))
  attr(dredge_global_gam$terms, ".Environment") <- 
    list2env(list(dredge_model_data = dredge_model_data))
  
  # Perform model selection
  cli::cli_alert_info("Dredging LM... (this may take a moment)")
  suppressMessages({
    top10_lm_models <- get.models(
      dredge(dredge_global_lm, trace = FALSE),
      subset = 1:10
    )
  })
  
  cli::cli_alert_info("Dredging GAM... (this may take a moment)")
  suppressMessages({
    top10_gam_models <- get.models(
      dredge(dredge_global_gam, trace = FALSE),
      subset = 1:10
    )
  })
  
  # Extract model formulas
  terms_lm <- lapply(top10_lm_models, function(m) m$terms)
  terms_gam <- lapply(top10_gam_models, function(m) m$formula)
  
  cli::cli_alert_success("Dredge pre-computation complete.")
  
  # --- Step 2: Run cross-validation ---
  set.seed(6)  # For reproducible splits
  
  Sys.time()
  
  cv_results <- run_all_models_cv(
    df = df_to_run,
    num_rounds = num_rounds,
    best_params_xgb = best_params_xgb,
    best_params_rf = best_params_rf,
    terms_lm = terms_lm,
    terms_gam = terms_gam,
    vip_threshold = vip_threshold,
    n_cores = n_cores
  )
  
  Sys.time()
  cli::cli_h1(paste("CV Analysis Complete for:", save_prefix))
  
  # --- Step 3: Summarize and display results ---
  cv_summary <- cv_results$all_cv_metrics %>%
    group_by(model_type, model_name) %>%
    summarize(
      mean_R2 = mean(R2),
      mean_RMSE = mean(RMSE),
      mean_RPD = mean(RPD),
      mean_Bias = mean(Bias),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(mean_RMSE)
  
  cat(paste(
    "\n--- OVERALL CV METRICS for", save_prefix,
    "(Mean of", num_rounds * 10, "runs) ---\n"
  ))
  print(cv_summary)
  
  # --- Step 4: Save results ---
  save_filename <- paste0(
    "Chapter 2/",
    save_prefix,
    "_",
    num_rounds,
    "x10_CV_results.RDS"
  )
  saveRDS(cv_results, save_filename)
  cli::cli_alert_success(paste("Results saved to:", save_filename))
  
  # Return results
  return(cv_results)
}
```


```{r}
# =============================================================================
# SECTION 7: UTILITY FUNCTIONS
# =============================================================================

#' Clean up parallel workers
#' 
#' Resets the parallel backend and clears any zombie worker processes.
#' Should be called before starting new parallel operations.
cleanup_parallel <- function() {
  
  # Reset to sequential processing
  future::plan(future::sequential)
  
  # Force garbage collection
  gc()
  
  # Kill zombie workers (Unix/Mac only)
  if (.Platform$OS.type == "unix") {
    system("pkill -f 'future::ClusterRegistry'", ignore.stderr = TRUE)
  }
  
  # Clear future registry
  if (exists(".future", envir = .GlobalEnv)) {
    rm(.future, envir = .GlobalEnv)
  }
  
  cli::cli_alert_success("Parallel workers cleaned up. Plan reset to sequential.")
  
  invisible(TRUE)
}
```

# Prepare metrics data with consistent naming
all_results_cleaned <- cv_metrics %>%
  mutate(

      model_name == "XGBoost" ~ "XGB",

      model_name == "Simple-LM (L+SW)" ~ "LM (Simple)",
      model_name == "Simple-GAM (L+SW)" ~ "GAM (Simple)",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    ModelType = case_when(

      model_type %in% c("PLS", "PLS-VIP") ~ "PLS",
      model_type %in% c("XGB", "RF") ~ "ML",
      model_type == "Simple" ~ "Simple",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Model)) %>%
  mutate(
    Model = factor(Model, levels = final_model_order),
    ModelType = factor(ModelType, levels = c("PCA", "PLS", "ML", "Simple"))
  )

#~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~#
# FIGURE 1: MODEL PERFORMANCE BOXPLOTS ####

create_boxplot <- function(data, y_var, y_lab, show_x_axis = FALSE) {
  y_var_q <- rlang::enquo(y_var)
  
  p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = Model, y = !!y_var_q, fill = ModelType)) +
    geom_boxplot(
      outlier.shape = 1,
      outlier.size = 1.3,
      outlier.alpha = 0.7,
      color = "black",
      width = 0.5,
      alpha = 0.8
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = color_palette) +
    scale_x_discrete(
      labels = function(x) str_replace(x, " \\(", "\n(")
    ) +
    labs(y = y_lab, x = NULL) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 15) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
  
  if (!show_x_axis) {
    p <- p + theme(
      axis.title.x = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x = element_blank()
    )
  }
  return(p)
}

p_rmse <- create_boxplot(all_results_cleaned, RMSE, "RMSE (Days)")
p_r2 <- create_boxplot(all_results_cleaned, R2, expression(R^2))
p_bias <- create_boxplot(all_results_cleaned, Bias, "Bias (Days)", show_x_axis = TRUE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "gray40", linewidth = 1, linetype = 2)
p_rpd <- create_boxplot(all_results_cleaned, RPD, "RPD", show_x_axis = TRUE)

# Create legend
legend_plot <- ggplot(all_results_cleaned, aes(x = Model, y = RMSE, fill = ModelType)) +
  geom_boxplot() + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = color_palette, name = "Model Type") + 
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.margin = margin(t = -12, unit = "pt"),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90"), 
    legend.text = element_text(size = 15.5),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 15.5)
  )

shared_legend <- get_legend(legend_plot)

# Combine plots
composite_plot <- arrangeGrob(
  arrangeGrob(p_rmse, p_r2, p_bias, p_rpd, nrow = 2),
  shared_legend,
  nrow = 2,
  heights = c(10, 1)
)

grid.arrange(composite_plot)

  filename = paste0("Chapter 2/", "model_comparison_boxplots_", region_prefix, "_", timestamp, ".png"),

)

  ) %>%

# Use a random sample from the dataset
specimen_proc_long <- scan_proc_long %>% filter(specimen == sample(unique(df$specimen), 1))

# Calculate absorbance range for scaling
ABS_MIN <- min(specimen_proc_long$absorbance, na.rm = TRUE)
ABS_MAX <- max(specimen_proc_long$absorbance, na.rm = TRUE)
ABS_RANGE <- ABS_MAX - ABS_MIN

# Prepare importance data

gam_comp <- str_extract(best_gam_name, "\\d+")

final_method_order_importance <- c(
  "PCA Loadings (LM)",
  "PCA Loadings (GAM)",
  "VIP Score (PLS)",
  "Gain (XGB)",
  "Permutation (RF)"
)

importance_summary <- importance_df %>%
  mutate(
    method = case_when(
      model_name == best_lm_name ~ "PCA Loadings (LM)",
      model_name == best_gam_name ~ "PCA Loadings (GAM)",
      model_name == "PLS-VIP" ~ "VIP Score (PLS)",
      model_name == "XGBoost" ~ "Gain (XGB)",
      model_name == "Random Forest" ~ "Permutation (RF)",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(method)) %>%
  group_by(method, wavenumber) %>%
  summarise(
    final_mean = mean(importance_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    lower_bound = mean(importance_mean - 2*importance_sd, na.rm = TRUE),
    upper_bound = mean(importance_mean + 2*importance_sd, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(method = factor(method, levels = final_method_order_importance))

# Extract data for plotting
lm_pca_data <- filter(importance_summary, method == "PCA Loadings (LM)")
gam_pca_data <- filter(importance_summary, method == "PCA Loadings (GAM)")
pls_data <- filter(importance_summary, method == "VIP Score (PLS)")
xgb_data <- filter(importance_summary, method == "Gain (XGB)")
rf_data <- filter(importance_summary, method == "Permutation (RF)")

# Universal overlay function
add_spectra_overlay <- function(plot_obj, importance_data) {
  I_MIN <- min(importance_data$final_mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  I_MAX <- max(importance_data$final_mean, na.rm = TRUE)
  I_RANGE <- I_MAX - I_MIN
  
  if (I_RANGE < 1e-6) {
    I_RANGE <- I_MAX
  }
  
  TARGET_A_RANGE_ON_I <- I_RANGE * 0.8
  m_abs <- TARGET_A_RANGE_ON_I / ABS_RANGE 
  
  I_CENTER <- (I_MAX + I_MIN) / 2
  A_CENTER <- (ABS_MAX + ABS_MIN) / 2
  c_abs <- I_CENTER - (m_abs * A_CENTER)
  
  plot_obj + 
    geom_line(
      data = specimen_proc_long,
      aes(y = absorbance * m_abs + c_abs),
      color = "grey", 
      alpha = 0.6, 
      linewidth = 0.7
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      name = plot_obj$labels$y,
      sec.axis = sec_axis(
        trans = ~ (. - c_abs) / m_abs, 
        name = NULL,
        breaks = NULL
      )
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 15) + 
    theme(
      axis.title.y.right = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y.right = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y.right = element_blank()
    )
}

# Prepare table data
table_data_full <- summary_table %>%
  mutate(
    Model = case_when(
      # model_name == best_lm_name ~ "LM",
      # model_name == best_gam_name ~ "GAM",
      model_name == "PLS" ~ "PLS",
      str_detect(model_name, "PLS-VIP") ~ "PLS-VIP",
      model_name == "XGBoost" ~ "XGB",
      model_name == "Random Forest" ~ "RF",
      model_name == "Simple-LM (L+SW)" ~ "Simple LM",
      model_name == "Simple-GAM (L+SW)" ~ "Simple GAM",
      str_detect(model_name, "PCA-LM") ~ model_name,  # Keep all PCA-LM variants
      str_detect(model_name, "PCA-GAM") ~ model_name, # Keep all PCA-GAM variants
      TRUE ~ model_name
    ),
    ModelType = case_when(
      model_type %in% c("PCA-LM", "PCA-GAM") ~ "PCA",
      model_type %in% c("PLS", "PLS-VIP") ~ "PLS",
      model_type %in% c("XGB", "RF") ~ "ML",
      model_type == "Simple" ~ "Simple",
      TRUE ~ model_type
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(RMSE)

max_abs_bias_full <- max(abs(table_data_full$Bias))

# Full colored table (all models)
table_to_export_full <- table_data_full %>%
  select(Model, RMSE, R2, Bias, RPD) %>%
  gt() %>%
  data_color(columns = RMSE, palette = c("#63BE7B", "#FFEB84", "#F8696B")) %>%
  data_color(columns = R2, palette = c("#F8696B", "#FFEB84", "#63BE7B")) %>%
  data_color(
    columns = Bias, 
    palette = c("#F8696B", "#63BE7B", "#F8696B"),

  ) %>%
  data_color(columns = RPD, palette = c("#F8696B", "#FFEB84", "#63BE7B")) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(RMSE, R2, Bias, RPD), decimals = 3) %>%

    column_labels.border.bottom.width = px(2),

  left_join(
    df %>% dplyr::select(specimen, sample_date, hatch_date), 
    by = "specimen"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Predicted hatch = sample date - predicted age
    pred_hatch = sample_date - pred_age,
    Model = case_when(
      model_name == best_lm_name ~ "LM",
      model_name == best_gam_name ~ "GAM",
      model_name == "PLS" ~ "PLS",
      str_detect(model_name, "PLS-VIP") ~ "PLS (VIP)",
      model_name == "XGBoost" ~ "XGB",
      model_name == "Random Forest" ~ "RF",
      model_name == "Simple-LM (L+SW)" ~ "LM (Simple)",
      model_name == "Simple-GAM (L+SW)" ~ "GAM (Simple)",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    ModelType = case_when(
      model_type %in% c("PCA-LM", "PCA-GAM") ~ "PCA",
      model_type %in% c("PLS", "PLS-VIP") ~ "PLS",
      model_type %in% c("XGB", "RF") ~ "ML",
      model_type == "Simple" ~ "Simple",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Model))

# Calculate median hatch date per specimen per model
median_hatch_estimates <- hatch_estimates %>%
  group_by(specimen, Model, ModelType, hatch_date) %>%
  summarise(median_pred_hatch = median(pred_hatch, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Get unique true hatch dates
true_hatch_dates <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(hatch_date)) %>%
  pull(hatch_date)

# K-S test and ECDF calculation
calculate_ecdf_diff <- function(estimate_dates, true_dates) {
  x_grid <- sort(unique(c(estimate_dates, true_dates)))
  ecdf_estimate <- ecdf(estimate_dates)(x_grid)
  ecdf_true <- ecdf(true_dates)(x_grid)
  tibble(
    hatch_date = x_grid, 
    ecdf_difference = ecdf_estimate - ecdf_true
  )
}

# Calculate K-S statistics for each model
ks_results <- median_hatch_estimates %>%
  group_by(Model, ModelType) %>%
  summarise(
    ks_data = list({
      ks_test <- ks.test(median_pred_hatch, true_hatch_dates)
      tibble(
        D_statistic = ks_test$statistic,
        p_value = ks_test$p.value
      )
    }),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(ks_data)

# Calculate ECDF differences
ecdf_differences <- median_hatch_estimates %>%
  group_by(Model, ModelType) %>%
  summarise(
    diff_data = list(calculate_ecdf_diff(median_pred_hatch, true_hatch_dates)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(diff_data) %>%
  left_join(ks_results, by = c("Model", "ModelType")) %>%
  mutate(
    p_label = if_else(p_value < 0.001, "p < 0.001", sprintf("p = %.3f", p_value)),
    ks_label = sprintf("D = %.3f\n%s", D_statistic, p_label),
    Model = factor(Model, levels = c("LM", "GAM", "PLS", "PLS (VIP)", "XGB", "RF", "LM (Simple)", "GAM (Simple)"))
  )

# Create ECDF difference plot
hatch_plot <- ggplot(ecdf_differences, aes(x = hatch_date, y = ecdf_difference)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black") +
  geom_step(aes(color = ModelType, group = Model), linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = ks_label), 
    x = -Inf, y = Inf, 
    hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.2,
    size = 4, 
    check_overlap = TRUE, 
    lineheight = 0.9
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = color_palette, name = "Model Type") +
  facet_wrap(~ Model, ncol = 4) +
  labs(
    x = "Hatch Date",
    y = "ECDF Difference"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 18) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.margin = margin(t = -5.5, unit = "pt"),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90")
  )

print(hatch_plot)

ggsave(
  filename = paste0("Chapter 2/", "hatch_comparison_", region_prefix, "_", timestamp, ".png"),
  plot = hatch_plot,
  width = 12,
  height = 8,
  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)
